scope: Nongovernmental US GAAP operating company and acquirer, calendar 2026, with separately identified private-company and SEC-registrant branches. Historical FASB pronouncements and issued amendments supply bounded research, not verification of the current consolidated Codification. Seller, investor, insurer, government, bankruptcy and tax conclusions are outside the selected answers.
common_gaps: The FASB Codification login returned no readable paragraphs on 2026-09-19. No terms were accepted, CAPTCHA bypassed or current consolidated text verified. Reused access-boundary record preserves the prior displayed-license findings without claiming they were reverified today.

Historical FASB Statements and Interpretations are superseded as authoritative literature by the Codification. ASUs communicate amendments. Current paragraph wording, later amendments and entity-specific adoption require a permitted current-text review.

No professional accounting or legal sign-off, actual agreement, valuation, claim file, environmental assessment or operational evidence was obtained. Proposed controls and synthetic approvals do not establish operating effectiveness.
External full text is not stored. Publisher copyright and unresolved automated-reuse and training permissions remain outside the project licenses.

sources.locator: 805-10-55-3A through 55-5F, 55-8 through 55-9 and 65-4; printed pp.3-4 and 6-10
sources.effective_period: Public business entities: annual periods beginning after 2017-12-15 including interim periods; other entities: annual periods after 2018-12-15 and interim periods within annual periods after 2019-12-15; prospective with specified early-application conditions.
sources.summary: The concentration screen can establish that an acquired set is not a business. Otherwise inputs and a substantive process must be assessed; continuing revenue alone is insufficient.
sources.classification: Issued amendment; not current consolidated authority

sources.effective_period: JV formation dates on or after 2025-01-01; early adoption permitted; earlier formations may elect retrospective application with sufficient information.
sources.summary: The venture's formation statements use a new basis, generally fair value with specified exceptions. This does not determine venturer investment accounting or redefine a joint venture.

sources.effective_period: Non-private entities: fiscal years after 2019-12-15 including interim periods; private companies: fiscal years after 2020-12-15 and interim periods within fiscal years after 2021-12-15; retrospective, early adoption permitted.
sources.summary: A qualifying private-company election applies to all eligible common-control entities, preserves other consolidation guidance and requires disclosures. Common ownership alone is insufficient.
sources.classification: Issued amendment; not current consolidated authority

sources.edition: March 1982; Original Pronouncements as Amended, copyright 2008
sources.locator: Paragraphs 1-5 and 24; FAS57 printed pp.2-3 and glossary
sources.effective_period: Historical effective date: fiscal years ending after 1982-06-15. Current application requires ASC 850 and relevant later guidance.
sources.summary: Relationships, transactions, balances and settlement terms require distinct evidence. An arm's-length claim needs substantiation; some control relationships matter without transactions.
sources.material_read: Official as-amended PDF disclosure, transition and glossary sections.

sources.title: FASB Statement 5: loss-contingency research
sources.effective_period: Historical pronouncement, effective 1975-07-01; current application requires ASC 450 and transaction-specific guidance.
sources.summary: Accrual depends on a probable incurred loss and reasonable estimation. Possible additional losses have separate disclosure requirements; general business-risk reserves are inappropriate.

sources.title: FASB Interpretation 45: guarantor recognition research
sources.effective_period: Initial recognition/measurement prospectively for guarantees issued or modified after 2002-12-31; disclosures for periods ending after 2002-12-15. Current ASC 460 and other applicable topics control.
sources.summary: An in-scope guarantee has a stand-ready obligation distinct from contingent payment. Initial fair-value recognition has exceptions, including specified related-party guarantees; disclosure scope is separate.
sources.material_read: Original PDF scope, exclusions, recognition/measurement, disclosure and effective-date paragraphs; as-amended URL returned an error, recovered original publisher PDF.

sources.title: FASB Statement 146: exit-cost research
sources.effective_period: Exit or disposal activities initiated after 2002-12-31; early application encouraged. Current ASC 420 and newer lease guidance require separate review.
sources.summary: Other exit costs arise when incurred, generally as goods or services are received. A plan alone does not create that liability; cost and liability movements require disclosure.
sources.material_read: Official PDF and publisher-indexed text for paragraphs 17-21. Older lease paragraphs are excluded from this package's treatment.

sources.summary: Discontinued-operation presentation requires the applicable disposal criteria and a strategic shift with a major effect; held-for-sale classification has separate conditions.

sources.title: FASB Statement 143: retirement versus remediation
sources.effective_period: Historical effective date: fiscal years beginning after 2002-06-15; current ASC 410-20, subsequent amendments and entity facts require review.
sources.summary: Legal retirement duties from normal asset operation are distinguished from improper-operation remediation. The model includes fair-value recognition, capitalized retirement cost, accretion, revisions and settlements.
sources.material_read: Original PDF scope, measurement, subsequent accounting, funding, disclosures and transition. Alternative as-amended PDF was intermittently inaccessible.

questions.question: US business versus asset acquisition: what facts must precede the residual calculation?
questions.answer: Evaluate concentration in a single or similar identifiable asset, then, if that screen does not exclude a business, the input and substantive-process criteria. Revenue continuity is insufficient. Identify buyer, control date, consideration, acquired processes and valuation evidence before assessing the acquisition method. The worked residual is arithmetic under explicit assumptions, not proof of goodwill recognition.
inputs: Executed purchase agreement and ownership/control memorandum
Acquisition-date consideration components, contingent terms and asset/liability valuation schedules
Organized workforce, process and output evidence; concentration-screen denominator
exceptions: Same-price single-asset purchase follows an asset-acquisition route; no automatic goodwill
Seller disposal, common-control transfer and JV formation are separate models
remaining_gaps: Complete current ASC 805 recognition, measurement exceptions, contingent consideration, tax effects, NCI and goodwill alternatives have not been verified; do not post the residual as goodwill solely from this packet.

questions.question: How do US joint-venture formation, investor accounting and formation dates differ?
questions.answer: First establish that the legal entity qualifies as a joint venture. The cited amendment addresses its own formation statements and new basis, regardless of whether contributed assets form a business. It does not decide a venturer's equity-method or consolidation accounting. A pre-2025 formation needs adoption evidence before using the later formation model.
inputs: Formation agreement and date the entity first meets the JV definition
Contributor interests, valuation of the venture and contributed net assets
Adoption election and sufficient historical information for any retrospective application
exceptions: Investor books cannot copy venture entries
A collaborative contract without a qualifying JV entity does not establish formation scope
remaining_gaps: Current consolidated 805-60 exceptions, formation measurement and actual JV qualification remain unverified; reuse guide-q-consolidation and guide-q-investments for separate investor research.

questions.question: Which US related-party evidence and common-control eligibility facts must remain separate?
questions.answer: Document ownership, management, relationships, services, balances and settlement terms, including unpriced transactions. Do not assert arm's-length terms without support. Separately assess the private-company VIE alternative: common control, no common control by a public business entity, a nonpublic counterparty and no controlling financial interest under the general model. The election covers all eligible entities and retains other guidance and disclosure duties.
inputs: Ownership and governance chart, management declarations and executed agreements
Both entities' balances, unbilled services and settlement terms
Private/public status, general-model control analysis and election memorandum
exceptions: A public-company parent fails the stated alternative eligibility
Separate statements and consolidated eliminations have different disclosure populations
remaining_gaps: Current ASC 850/810 text, common-control determination, measurement and completeness of actual related parties require review; no consolidation conclusion is supplied.

questions.question: How should a US claim estimate distinguish accrual, disclosure and later revisions?
questions.answer: The historical loss model requires a probable incurred loss at the balance date and a reasonable estimate for accrual. A reasonably possible additional loss has a distinct disclosure route, including inability to estimate. Keep the information date, balance date and estimate version. A general reserve or preferred earnings result cannot establish the obligation.
inputs: Legal correspondence, claim chronology and financial-statement issuance date
Probability assessment, supported estimate or range and counterevidence
Prior estimate and new information with reviewer disposition
exceptions: A merely possible claim is not automatically the same accrual
New post-balance-date events need separate subsequent-event analysis
remaining_gaps: Current ASC 450 range-selection and discounting rules, unasserted claims and litigation facts require review; no automatic midpoint/minimum rule is supplied.

questions.question: Why can a US guarantee require recognition when payment is not probable?
questions.answer: An in-scope guarantee includes a stand-ready obligation at inception, distinct from the payment contingency. The historical model uses fair value, subject to its measurement provisions. First check exclusions: product warranties, certain related-party guarantees, derivatives and business-combination consideration do not all follow the same initial-recognition route; disclosure may still apply.
inputs: Signed guarantee, beneficiary, maximum exposure, term and recourse
Relationship and scope-exception analysis
Premium or fair-value support and separate contingent-loss assessment
exceptions: Remote payment does not by itself eliminate an in-scope stand-ready liability
Parent/subsidiary guarantees must not inherit the unrelated-party fixture
remaining_gaps: Current ASC 460, initial measurement interaction with loss contingencies, subsequent measurement and exception-specific disclosure remain unverified.

questions.question: How should a US policyholder insurance recovery remain separate from a claim liability?
questions.answer: Assess the claim and potential recovery separately; the $100,000 liability estimate does not establish a $60,000 asset or permission to report a $40,000 liability. Record policy coverage, deductibles, insurer response and collectibility. In the distinct SEC-registrant branch, Topic 5.Y footnote 49 presumes against a recovery asset when the indemnifying party denies liability unless rebutted with support and disclosure. The base fixture leaves the contested recovery unrecognized.
inputs: Policy version, insured event, exclusions, deductible, limit and notice compliance
Insurer coverage decision and solvency evidence
Separate liability and recovery conclusions with dates and approvals
exceptions: Policyholder is not insurer; insurer reserve accounting is outside scope
SEC staff interpretation is not asserted as universal private-company authority
Later collection or changed evidence does not retroactively establish the original asset
remaining_gaps: Permitted current-text review of recovery recognition and balance-sheet/income-statement offset criteria is still needed. This packet demonstrates separate decisions, not a blanket gross-presentation rule or a complete insurance-recovery model.

questions.question: Which US exit costs arise from incurred services rather than a restructuring budget?
questions.answer: For the selected other-exit-cost branch, record received goods or services and the resulting liability when incurred. A closure plan alone does not recognize future relocation services. Keep cost categories, cash settlements and estimate changes in a liability rollforward with the activity description and expected completion date.
inputs: Dated approval and closure plan
Service completion and vendor invoice evidence
Beginning liability, incurred costs, settlements, changes and disclosure schedule
exceptions: One-time termination benefits and lease termination require their own guidance
Bankruptcy and liquidation accounting are not established by a closure budget
remaining_gaps: Current ASC 420, termination-benefit conditions, ASC 842 lease exits and insolvency models remain outside the selected other-cost answer.

questions.question: Does a US disposal plan automatically qualify as a discontinued operation?
questions.answer: No. Assess the applicable disposal or held-for-sale route separately from whether the component's disposal is a strategic shift with a major effect on operations and financial results. Held-for-sale evidence includes commitment, immediate availability, an active buyer program, probable timely sale, reasonable marketing price and unlikely significant plan changes. A routine machine sale does not alone establish the strategic-shift criterion.
inputs: Component and asset-group definitions
Approval, marketing, buyer and sale-timing evidence
Quantitative and qualitative strategic-shift assessment
exceptions: A budget to sell is not all held-for-sale criteria
Abandonment and acquired businesses held for sale have distinct branches
remaining_gaps: Current ASC 205-20/360 measurement, impairment sequence, exceptions to sale timing and actual major-effect assessment require review; capital-asset foundation #120 supplies adjacent research.

questions.question: Retirement versus remediation: which US legal and accounting facts determine the obligation route?
questions.answer: Separate a legal duty from normal acquisition, construction or operation of a tangible asset from improper-operation remediation. Under the historical retirement model, recognize an estimable fair-value obligation and related asset cost, then reconcile accretion, revisions and settlements. EPA responsible-party categories identify legal investigation needs; they do not themselves supply a GAAP liability amount. Remediation discounting must not copy the retirement model automatically.
inputs: Asset/site identity, legal duty, permit or contract and operating history
Engineering cash-flow timing, probabilities, rate and estimate version
Owner/operator/arranger/transporter facts, notices, defenses and other responsible parties
exceptions: Accidental contamination from improper operation is a remediation route
Insurer funding or a guarantee does not alone extinguish the retirement obligation
Environmental credits and regulated-utility accounting are separate questions
remaining_gaps: Current ASC 410-20/410-30, conditional retirement duties, legal defenses, site remediation allocation and permitted discounting require specialist and current-authority review. EPA guidance is explanatory, not the complete statute.
